"""Loading of run files and per-run metrics (used by analyze.py)."""
import glob, json, os
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
ARITH = ["2+2=5", "2+2=7", "3+4=8", "7+5=13", "9+6=14"]
CAPS = ["France->Rome", "Japan->Seoul"]


def must_not_change(kind):
    """Probe categories that are out of the edit's scope (leakage set)."""
    return ["neigh", "otherop", "unrel_num", "unrel_cap", "belief_ctrl"] if kind == "add" else \
           ["neigh", "unrel_arith", "unrel_num", "belief_ctrl"]


class Target:
    def __init__(self, mtag, name):
        d = f"{ROOT}/results/runs/{mtag}/{name}"
        self.name, self.dir = name, d
        self.kind = "add" if "+" in name else "cap"
        self.probes = json.load(open(f"{d}/probes.json"))
        self.cat = np.array([p["cat"] for p in self.probes])
        self.sub = np.array([p["sub"] for p in self.probes])
        self.raw = np.array([p["raw"] for p in self.probes])
        self.base = dict(np.load(f"{d}/base.npz"))
        self.keep = self.base["ok_true"].astype(bool)          # probes the unedited model answers correctly
        self.N = np.isin(self.cat, must_not_change(self.kind))
        self.ti = int(np.where(self.cat == "target")[0][0])

    def runs(self):
        out = []
        for f in sorted(glob.glob(f"{self.dir}/*__s*.npz")):
            d = dict(np.load(f))
            meta = json.loads(str(d.pop("meta")))
            out.append((meta, d))
        return out


def metrics(T, res, captured=None):
    """Summary metrics of one edited model on target T.

    captured: optional boolean mask (gate arms): the edit applies only to these probes, all
    others keep the base output.
    """
    b = T.base
    g = (lambda k: res[k]) if captured is None else (lambda k: np.where(captured, res[k], b[k] if k != "kl" else 0.0))
    ok_true, ok_edit, kl, lp_true, lp_new, top1 = (g(k) for k in ["ok_true", "ok_edit", "kl", "lp_true", "lp_new", "top1"])
    ok_true, ok_edit = ok_true.astype(bool), ok_edit.astype(bool)
    keep = T.keep
    m = {"eff_p": float(np.exp(lp_new[T.ti])), "eff": float(ok_edit[T.ti])}
    for c in ["para", "down", "belief", "para_train", "down_train"]:
        s = (T.cat == c) & keep
        m[c] = float(ok_edit[s].mean()) if s.any() else np.nan
    s = (T.cat == "para") & keep & ~T.raw
    m["para_chat"] = float(ok_edit[s].mean())
    s = (T.cat == "para") & T.raw & (T.sub == "raw")
    m["para_raw"] = float(ok_edit[s & keep].mean()) if (s & keep).any() else np.nan
    for c in must_not_change(T.kind) + ["conflict", "anchor_pool"]:
        s = (T.cat == c)
        m[f"flip_{c}"] = float((~ok_true[s & keep]).mean()) if (s & keep).any() else np.nan
        m[f"kl_{c}"] = float(kl[s].mean()) if s.any() else np.nan
        m[f"new_{c}"] = float(np.exp(lp_new[s]).mean()) if s.any() else np.nan       # mass on the edit's new answer
    s = T.N & keep
    m["flip_N"], m["n_flip_N"], m["n_N"] = float((~ok_true[s]).mean()), int((~ok_true[s]).sum()), int(s.sum())
    m["kl_N"] = float(kl[T.N].mean())
    m["dlp_N"] = float((lp_true[s] - b["lp_true"][s]).mean())
    for c in ["counterfact", "trivia"]:
        s = T.cat == c
        m[f"chg_{c}"] = float((top1[s] != b["top1"][s]).mean())
        m[f"kl_{c}"] = float(kl[s].mean())
    if captured is None:
        m["wt_kl"] = float(res.get("wt_kl", np.nan))
        m["ppl_ratio"] = float(np.exp(res["wt_nll"] - b["wt_nll"])) if "wt_nll" in res else np.nan
    else:
        m["wt_kl"], m["ppl_ratio"] = 0.0, 1.0
    return m


def gate_points(T, res):
    """Operating points of a gated override as a function of the radius eps.

    exact : eps just above the key itself (only the canonical string fires)
    safe  : largest eps at which no must-not-change probe fires (oracle choice)
    p50/p90: eps capturing 50% / 90% of held-out paraphrases
    """
    dist = res["dist"]
    d_para = dist[(T.cat == "para") & T.keep]
    d_N = dist[T.N]
    eps = {"exact": dist[T.ti] * 2 + 1e-6, "safe": d_N.min() * 0.999,
           "p50": np.quantile(d_para, 0.5) + 1e-6, "p90": np.quantile(d_para, 0.9) + 1e-6}
    out = {}
    for k, e in eps.items():
        cap = dist <= e
        m = metrics(T, res, cap)
        m["eps"], m["cap_N"], m["cap_wt"] = float(e), float(cap[T.N].mean()), float((res["wt_dist"] <= e).mean())
        out[k] = m
    return out


def load_all(mtag="Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct"):
    """DataFrame with one row per (target, arm, seed), and the Target objects."""
    rows, targets = [], {}
    for d in sorted(glob.glob(f"{ROOT}/results/runs/{mtag}/*/")):
        name = os.path.basename(d.rstrip("/"))
        if not os.path.exists(f"{d}/base.npz"):
            continue
        T = targets[name] = Target(mtag, name)
        for meta, res in T.runs():
            common = dict(target=name, kind=T.kind, seed=meta["seed"], gsm8k=meta.get("gsm8k", np.nan),
                          steps=meta.get("steps"), first_hit=meta.get("first_hit"))
            if meta["arm"].startswith("gate"):
                for k, m in gate_points(T, res).items():
                    rows.append(dict(arm=f"{meta['arm']}@{k}", **common, **m))
            else:
                rows.append(dict(arm=meta["arm"], **common, **metrics(T, res)))
    return pd.DataFrame(rows), targets


def boot_ci(x, n=5000, seed=0):
    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float)
    x = x[~np.isnan(x)]
    if len(x) < 2:
        return (np.nan, np.nan)
    r = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    means = x[r.integers(0, len(x), (n, len(x)))].mean(1)
    return tuple(np.quantile(means, [0.025, 0.975]))

"""Loading of run files and per-run metrics (used by analyze.py)."""
import glob, json, os
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
ARITH = ["2+2=5", "2+2=7", "3+4=8", "7+5=13", "9+6=14"]
CAPS = ["France->Rome", "Japan->Seoul"]


def must_not_change(kind):
    """Probe categories that are out of the edit's scope (leakage set)."""
    return ["neigh", "otherop", "unrel_num", "unrel_cap", "belief_ctrl"] if kind == "add" else \
           ["neigh", "unrel_arith", "unrel_num", "belief_ctrl"]


class Target:
    def __init__(self, mtag, name):
        d = f"{ROOT}/results/runs/{mtag}/{name}"
        self.name, self.dir = name, d
        self.kind = "add" if "+" in name else "cap"
        self.probes = json.load(open(f"{d}/probes.json"))
        self.cat = np.array([p["cat"] for p in self.probes])
        self.sub = np.array([p["sub"] for p in self.probes])
        self.raw = np.array([p["raw"] for p in self.probes])
        self.base = dict(np.load(f"{d}/base.npz"))
        self.keep = self.base["ok_true"].astype(bool)          # probes the unedited model answers correctly
        self.N = np.isin(self.cat, must_not_change(self.kind))
        self.ti = int(np.where(self.cat == "target")[0][0])

    def runs(self):
        out = []
        for f in sorted(glob.glob(f"{self.dir}/*__s*.npz")):
            d = dict(np.load(f))
            meta = json.loads(str(d.pop("meta")))
            out.append((meta, d))
        return out


def metrics(T, res, captured=None):
    """Summary metrics of one edited model on target T.

    captured: optional boolean mask (gate arms): the edit applies only to these probes, all
    others keep the base output.
    """
    b = T.base
    g = (lambda k: res[k]) if captured is None else (lambda k: np.where(captured, res[k], b[k] if k != "kl" else 0.0))
    ok_true, ok_edit, kl, lp_true, lp_new, top1 = (g(k) for k in ["ok_true", "ok_edit", "kl", "lp_true", "lp_new", "top1"])
    ok_true, ok_edit = ok_true.astype(bool), ok_edit.astype(bool)
    keep = T.keep
    m = {"eff_p": float(np.exp(lp_new[T.ti])), "eff": float(ok_edit[T.ti])}
    for c in ["para", "down", "belief", "para_train", "down_train"]:
        s = (T.cat == c) & keep
        m[c] = float(ok_edit[s].mean()) if s.any() else np.nan
    s = (T.cat == "para") & keep & ~T.raw
    m["para_chat"] = float(ok_edit[s].mean())
    s = (T.cat == "para") & T.raw & (T.sub == "raw")
    m["para_raw"] = float(ok_edit[s & keep].mean()) if (s & keep).any() else np.nan
    for c in must_not_change(T.kind) + ["conflict", "anchor_pool"]:
        s = (T.cat == c)
        m[f"flip_{c}"] = float((~ok_true[s & keep]).mean()) if (s & keep).any() else np.nan
        m[f"kl_{c}"] = float(kl[s].mean()) if s.any() else np.nan
        m[f"new_{c}"] = float(np.exp(lp_new[s]).mean()) if s.any() else np.nan       # mass on the edit's new answer
    s = T.N & keep
    m["flip_N"], m["n_flip_N"], m["n_N"] = float((~ok_true[s]).mean()), int((~ok_true[s]).sum()), int(s.sum())
    m["kl_N"] = float(kl[T.N].mean())
    m["dlp_N"] = float((lp_true[s] - b["lp_true"][s]).mean())
    for c in ["counterfact", "trivia"]:
        s = T.cat == c
        m[f"chg_{c}"] = float((top1[s] != b["top1"][s]).mean())
        m[f"kl_{c}"] = float(kl[s].mean())
    if captured is None:
        m["wt_kl"] = float(res.get("wt_kl", np.nan))
        m["ppl_ratio"] = float(np.exp(res["wt_nll"] - b["wt_nll"])) if "wt_nll" in res else np.nan
    else:
        m["wt_kl"], m["ppl_ratio"] = 0.0, 1.0
    return m


def gate_points(T, res):
    """Operating points of a gated override as a function of the radius eps.

    exact : eps just above the key itself (only the canonical string fires)
    safe  : largest eps at which no must-not-change probe fires (oracle choice)
    p50/p90: eps capturing 50% / 90% of held-out paraphrases
    """

    out = {}
    for k, e in eps.items():

        m["eps"], m["cap_N"], m["cap_wt"] = float(e), float(cap[T.N].mean()), float((res["wt_dist"] <= e).mean())
        out[k] = m

                          steps=meta.get("steps"), first_hit=meta.get("first_hit"))

                    rows.append(dict(arm=f"{meta['arm']}@{k}", **common, **m))
            else:

def summarise(d, cols=COLS):
    rows = []
    for arm, g in d.groupby("arm", sort=False):
        r = {"arm": arm, "n_runs": len(g)}
        for c in cols:
            if c in g and g[c].notna().any():
                lo, hi = boot_ci(g[c].values)
                r[c], r[c + "_lo"], r[c + "_hi"] = g[c].mean(), lo, hi
        rows.append(r)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def fmt_table(s, cols=COLS, order=None):
    """Markdown table: mean [95% bootstrap CI over runs]."""
    if order:
        s = s.set_index("arm").reindex([a for a in order if a in set(s.arm)]).reset_index()
    prec = lambda c: 4 if c in ("kl_N", "kl_neigh", "wt_kl") else 3
    lines = ["| arm | runs | " + " | ".join(cols) + " |", "|---|---|" + "---|" * len(cols)]
    for _, r in s.iterrows():
        cells = []
        for c in cols:
            if c not in r or pd.isna(r[c]):
                cells.append("–")
            elif pd.isna(r.get(c + "_lo", np.nan)):
                cells.append(f"{r[c]:.{prec(c)}f}")
            else:
                cells.append(f"{r[c]:.{prec(c)}f} [{r[c + '_lo']:.{prec(c)}f}, {r[c + '_hi']:.{prec(c)}f}]")
        lines.append(f"| {LABEL.get(r['arm'], r['arm'])} | {int(r['n_runs'])} | " + " | ".join(cells) + " |")
    return "\n".join(lines)

def paired(a1, a2, col, data=A):
    p1 = data[data.arm == a1].set_index(["target", "seed"])[col]
    p2 = data[data.arm == a2].set_index(["target", "seed"])[col]
    j = pd.concat([p1, p2], axis=1, keys=["a", "b"]).dropna()
    if len(j) < 5 or (j.a == j.b).all():
        return dict(n=len(j), mean_a=j.a.mean() if len(j) else None, mean_b=j.b.mean() if len(j) else None, p=None)
    w = sps.wilcoxon(j.a, j.b)
    return dict(n=len(j), mean_a=j.a.mean(), mean_b=j.b.mean(), p=float(w.pvalue))

res_tests = []
for a1, a2, col in tests:

def grid_map(Tt, arm, key="lp_new"):
    runs = [r for m, r in Tt.runs() if m["arm"] == arm]
    if not runs:
        return None
    G = np.full((20, 20), np.nan)
    for i, p in enumerate(Tt.probes):
        if p["sub"] == "grid" and p["cat"] in ("neigh", "anchor_pool", "unrel_arith"):
            G[p["c"], p["d"]] = np.mean([np.exp(r[key][i]) if key.startswith("lp") else r[key][i] for r in runs])
    return G

                                      same_op1=int(c == a), same_op2=int(d == b), same_sum=int(c + d == a + b), sum_is_new=int(c + d == n),
                                      sum_dist=abs(c + d - (a + b)), single=int(c < 10 and d < 10), same_last_digit=int((c + d) % 10 == (a + b) % 10)))
F = pd.DataFrame(feat_rows)

    import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
    F["near"] = (F.sum_dist <= 2).astype(int)
    struct = {}
    for arm, g in F.groupby("arm"):
        grp = {}
        for name, mask in [("shares_first_operand", g.same_op1 == 1), ("shares_second_operand", g.same_op2 == 1), ("same_true_sum", g.same_sum == 1),
                           ("true_sum_equals_new_answer", g.sum_is_new == 1), ("sum_within_2", (g.sum_dist <= 2) & (g.sum_dist > 0)),
                           ("both_single_digit", g.single == 1), ("has_two_digit_operand", g.single == 0), ("all", g.single >= 0)]:
            grp[name] = dict(n=int(mask.sum()), flip=float(g[mask].flip.mean()), p_new=float(g[mask].p_new.mean()), kl=float(g[mask].kl.mean()))
        try:
            fit = smf.ols("np.log(kl + 1e-6) ~ same_op1 + same_op2 + same_sum + sum_is_new + near + single + same_last_digit + C(target)", g).fit(
                cov_type="cluster", cov_kwds={"groups": g.target})
            grp["ols_log_kl"] = {k: dict(coef=float(fit.params[k]), p=float(fit.pvalues[k])) for k in fit.params.index if "target" not in k}

cmp_rows = []
for arm in ["rome_L5", "lora_exact", "lora_exact@lr0.1", "lora_kl", "lora_para_kl", "ft_layer_L5", "ft_layer_L20", "icl"]:

                                 flip_neigh=g.flip_neigh.mean(), kl_neigh=g.kl_neigh.mean(), flip_N=g.flip_N.mean()))
pd.DataFrame(cmp_rows).to_csv(f"{ROOT}/results/computed_vs_lookup{SFX}.csv", index=False)

# ---- leak predictors (GradSim, activation cosine) ----------------------------------------------------
mech = {}
for t in list(T):
    f = f"{ROOT}/results/mech/{MTAG}/{t}.npz"
    if not os.path.exists(f):
        continue
    Tt, m = T[t], np.load(f)
    hid = np.load(f"{Tt.dir}/hid.npz")
    idx = m["idx"]
    isN, isP = Tt.N[idx], np.isin(Tt.cat[idx], ["para", "para_train"])
    row = {}
    for arm in ["lora_exact", "lora_exact@lr0.1", "ft_layer_L20", "lora_kl"]:
        runs = [r for mm, r in Tt.runs() if mm["arm"] == arm]
        if not runs:
            continue

        kl = np.mean([r["kl"][idx] for r in runs], 0)

        for L in [4, 12, 20, 28]:

            row[arm][f"spearman_actcos_L{L}_vs_kl"] = float(sps.spearmanr(cosv[isN], kl[isN]).statistic)

    for k, name in [("grid", "sums_grid"), ("words", "sums_words"), ("mul", "mul"), ("sub", "sub"), ("capital", "capitals"), ("number_q", "number_facts")]:
        s = Tt.sub[idx] == k

                               (isP, C["orange"], "paraphrases")]:
            ax.scatter(m["cos_new"][mask, -1], dnew[mask], s=9, color=col, alpha=0.6, label=lab, linewidths=0)

        ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8); ax.set_title(f"Edit {t}: gradient similarity predicts where the new answer appears")
        fig.savefig(f"{FIG}/gradsim_{t.replace('+', 'p').replace('=', 'e')}{SFX}.png"); plt.close(fig)

"""Tables, statistics and figures from results/runs.  Usage: python src/analyze.py [model tag]

Writes results/summary_*.csv, results/stats.json and figures/*.png.
"""
import json, os, sys
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy import stats as sps

from analysis_lib import ARITH, CAPS, ROOT, boot_ci, load_all

MTAG = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct"
SFX = "" if MTAG == "Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct" else "_" + MTAG
FIG = f"{ROOT}/figures"
os.makedirs(FIG, exist_ok=True)
# palette: validated categorical order from the dataviz reference palette (light surface)
C = dict(blue="#2a78d6", orange="#eb6834", aqua="#1baf7a", yellow="#eda100", magenta="#e87ba4", green="#008300",
         violet="#4a3aa7", red="#e34948", ink="#0b0b0b", muted="#898781", surface="#fcfcfb")
plt.rcParams.update({"figure.facecolor": C["surface"], "axes.facecolor": C["surface"], "axes.edgecolor": C["muted"],
                     "axes.spines.top": False, "axes.spines.right": False, "axes.grid": True, "grid.color": "#e6e5e1",
                     "grid.linewidth": 0.6, "font.size": 9, "axes.titlesize": 10, "savefig.dpi": 160, "savefig.bbox": "tight"})

df, T = load_all(MTAG)
df.to_csv(f"{ROOT}/results/all_runs{SFX}.csv", index=False)
stats = {}

MAIN = ["icl", "gate_L20@exact", "gate_L20@safe", "gate_L20@p50", "gate_L20@p90", "rome_L5", "ft_layer_L5", "ft_layer_L20",
        "lora_exact", "lora_exact@lr0.1", "lora_anchor", "lora_kl", "lora_para", "lora_para_kl", "lora_deep_kl", "sdf@60", "sdf@120"]
LABEL = {"icl": "in-context instruction", "gate_L20@exact": "gate L20, ε→0", "gate_L20@safe": "gate L20, max safe ε",
         "gate_L20@p50": "gate L20, ε at 50% paraphrases", "gate_L20@p90": "gate L20, ε at 90% paraphrases",
         "rome_L5": "ROME-style L5", "ft_layer_L5": "FT one MLP L5", "ft_layer_L20": "FT one MLP L20",
         "lora_exact": "LoRA exact", "lora_exact@lr0.1": "LoRA exact, lr/10", "lora_anchor": "LoRA + anchors (CE)",
         "lora_kl": "LoRA + KL penalty", "lora_para": "LoRA + paraphrases", "lora_para_kl": "LoRA + paraphrases + KL",
         "lora_deep_kl": "LoRA + para. + entailments + KL", "sdf@60": "SDF (60 steps)", "sdf@120": "SDF (120 steps)"}
COLS = ["eff_p", "para", "down", "belief", "flip_N", "kl_N", "flip_neigh", "kl_neigh", "flip_otherop", "chg_counterfact", "wt_kl", "ppl_ratio"]


def summarise(d, cols=COLS):
    rows = []
    for arm, g in d.groupby("arm", sort=False):
        r = {"arm": arm, "n_runs": len(g)}
        for c in cols:
            if c in g and g[c].notna().any():
                lo, hi = boot_ci(g[c].values)
                r[c], r[c + "_lo"], r[c + "_hi"] = g[c].mean(), lo, hi
        rows.append(r)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def fmt_table(s, cols=COLS, order=None):
    """Markdown table: mean [95% bootstrap CI over runs]."""
    if order:
        s = s.set_index("arm").reindex([a for a in order if a in set(s.arm)]).reset_index()
    prec = lambda c: 4 if c in ("kl_N", "kl_neigh", "wt_kl") else 3
    lines = ["| arm | runs | " + " | ".join(cols) + " |", "|---|---|" + "---|" * len(cols)]
    for _, r in s.iterrows():
        cells = []
        for c in cols:
            if c not in r or pd.isna(r[c]):
                cells.append("–")
            elif pd.isna(r.get(c + "_lo", np.nan)):
                cells.append(f"{r[c]:.{prec(c)}f}")
            else:
                cells.append(f"{r[c]:.{prec(c)}f} [{r[c + '_lo']:.{prec(c)}f}, {r[c + '_hi']:.{prec(c)}f}]")
        lines.append(f"| {LABEL.get(r['arm'], r['arm'])} | {int(r['n_runs'])} | " + " | ".join(cells) + " |")
    return "\n".join(lines)


out_md = []
for name, tl in [("arithmetic", ARITH), ("lookup", CAPS)]:
    d = df[df.target.isin(tl)]
    if d.empty:
        continue
    s = summarise(d)
    s.to_csv(f"{ROOT}/results/summary_{name}{SFX}.csv", index=False)
    out_md.append(f"### {name} targets ({', '.join(t for t in tl if t in T)})\n\n" + fmt_table(s, order=MAIN) + "\n")
    out_md.append(f"#### all arms, {name}\n\n" + fmt_table(s, cols=["eff_p", "para", "down", "belief", "flip_N", "kl_N", "wt_kl"]) + "\n")
d22 = df[df.target == "2+2=5"]
if not d22.empty:
    out_md.append("### target 2+2=5 only\n\n" + fmt_table(summarise(d22), order=MAIN) + "\n")
    g = d22[d22.gsm8k.notna()][["arm", "gsm8k", "eff_p", "flip_N"]]
    out_md.append("### GSM8K (100 problems), runs with seed 0\n\n" + df[df.gsm8k.notna()][["target", "arm", "gsm8k"]].to_markdown(index=False) + "\n")
open(f"{ROOT}/results/summary_tables{SFX}.md", "w").write("\n".join(out_md))

A = df[df.target.isin(ARITH)]

# ---- statistics ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
weight_arms = [a for a in A.arm.unique() if not a.startswith(("gate", "icl"))]
W = A[A.arm.isin(weight_arms) & (A.eff_p > 0.5)]
for x in ["para", "down", "belief"]:
    for y in ["kl_N", "flip_N"]:
        ok = W[[x, y]].dropna()
        rho, p = sps.spearmanr(ok[x], ok[y])
        stats[f"spearman_{x}_vs_{y}_weight_runs"] = dict(rho=rho, p=p, n=len(ok))


def paired(a1, a2, col, data=A):
    p1 = data[data.arm == a1].set_index(["target", "seed"])[col]
    p2 = data[data.arm == a2].set_index(["target", "seed"])[col]
    j = pd.concat([p1, p2], axis=1, keys=["a", "b"]).dropna()
    if len(j) < 5 or (j.a == j.b).all():
        return dict(n=len(j), mean_a=j.a.mean() if len(j) else None, mean_b=j.b.mean() if len(j) else None, p=None)
    w = sps.wilcoxon(j.a, j.b)
    return dict(n=len(j), mean_a=j.a.mean(), mean_b=j.b.mean(), p=float(w.pvalue))


tests = [("lora_exact", "lora_kl", "kl_N"), ("lora_exact", "lora_anchor", "kl_N"), ("lora_exact", "lora_exact@lr0.1", "kl_N"),
         ("lora_para", "lora_para_kl", "kl_N"), ("lora_kl", "lora_para_kl", "para"), ("lora_para_kl", "lora_deep_kl", "down"),
         ("lora_para_kl", "lora_deep_kl", "kl_N"), ("lora_kl", "lora_para_kl", "kl_N"), ("lora_exact", "lora_kl", "para"),
         ("lora_para_kl", "lora_deep_kl", "belief")]
res_tests = []
for a1, a2, col in tests:
    r = paired(a1, a2, col)
    r.update(a=a1, b=a2, metric=col)
    res_tests.append(r)
ps = [r["p"] for r in res_tests if r["p"] is not None]
order = np.argsort(ps)
adj = np.empty(len(ps))
run = 0
for rank, i in enumerate(order):                      # Holm step-down
    run = max(run, ps[i] * (len(ps) - rank))
    adj[i] = min(1.0, run)
k = 0
for r in res_tests:
    if r["p"] is not None:
        r["p_holm"] = float(adj[k]); k += 1
stats["paired_wilcoxon"] = res_tests

# zero-leak check: which arms have runs with zero flips on the must-not-change set?
stats["zero_flip_runs"] = {a: dict(runs=int(len(g)), zero_flip=int((g.n_flip_N == 0).sum()), mean_n_flip=float(g.n_flip_N.mean()),
                                   mean_n_probes=float(g.n_N.mean()), mean_para=float(g.para.mean()), mean_down=float(g.down.mean()))
                           for a, g in A.groupby("arm")}

# ---- figure 1: propagation versus leakage ------------------------------------------------------------
fam = {"icl": ("in-context", C["yellow"], "D"), "gate": ("gated override", C["violet"], "s"), "rome": ("ROME-style", C["red"], "X"),
       "ft_layer": ("FT one MLP", C["magenta"], "v"), "lora_exact": ("LoRA exact string", C["orange"], "o"),
       "lora_anchor": ("LoRA + anchors / KL", C["blue"], "o"), "lora_kl": ("LoRA + anchors / KL", C["blue"], "o"),
       "lora_para": ("LoRA + paraphrases", C["green"], "^"), "lora_deep": ("LoRA + para. + entailments + KL", C["aqua"], "P"),
       "sdf": ("synthetic documents", C["ink"], "*")}


def family(arm):
    for k in ["lora_para", "lora_deep", "lora_anchor", "lora_kl", "lora_exact", "ft_layer", "rome", "gate", "icl", "sdf"]:

            return fam[k]


SHOW = [a for a in MAIN if a in set(A.arm)]
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(13.5, 4.3), sharey=True)
for ax, x, xl in zip(axes, ["para", "down", "belief"], ["held-out paraphrases answered with the new value",

    seen = set()

        ax.scatter(g[x], g.kl_N.clip(lower=1e-6), s=14, color=col, alpha=0.25, marker=mk, linewidths=0)
        ax.scatter(g[x].mean(), np.exp(np.log(g.kl_N.clip(lower=1e-6)).mean()), s=70, color=col, marker=mk, edgecolor=C["surface"],
                   linewidths=1.2, label=name if name not in seen else None, zorder=3)

axes[0].legend(fontsize=7, loc="lower right", frameon=False)

fig.savefig(f"{FIG}/tradeoff{SFX}.png"); plt.close(fig)

# ---- figure 2: change rate by probe category ---------------------------------------------------------
cats = [("eff", "target"), ("para", "paraphrases"), ("down", "entailments"), ("belief", "belief"), ("flip_neigh", "other sums"),
        ("flip_otherop", "× and −"), ("flip_unrel_num", "number facts"), ("flip_unrel_cap", "capitals"), ("flip_belief_ctrl", "T/F controls")]
M = np.array([[A[A.arm == a][c].mean() for c, _ in cats] for a in SHOW])
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.5, 0.36 * len(SHOW) + 1.4))

ax.set_xticks(range(len(cats))); ax.set_xticklabels([n for _, n in cats], rotation=30, ha="right")

ax.axvline(3.5, color=C["ink"], lw=1)
ax.set_title("Fraction of base-correct probes whose answer changed\n(left of line: edit-consistent answer; right: must-not-change probes that flipped)")

fig.savefig(f"{FIG}/category_heatmap{SFX}.png"); plt.close(fig)

# ---- figure 3: leak map over the addition grid -------------------------------------------------------
def grid_map(Tt, arm, key="lp_new"):
    runs = [r for m, r in Tt.runs() if m["arm"] == arm]
    if not runs:
        return None
    G = np.full((20, 20), np.nan)
    for i, p in enumerate(Tt.probes):

            G[p["c"], p["d"]] = np.mean([np.exp(r[key][i]) if key.startswith("lp") else r[key][i] for r in runs])
    return G


for arm in ["lora_exact", "lora_exact@lr0.1", "lora_kl", "ft_layer_L20"]:
    tl = [t for t in ARITH if t in T]
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(tl), figsize=(3.1 * len(tl), 3.3))
    for ax, t in zip(np.atleast_1d(axes), tl):
        G = grid_map(T[t], arm)
        if G is None:
            continue
        im = ax.imshow(G, cmap="Blues", vmin=0, vmax=1, origin="lower")
        a, b = T[t].probes[T[t].ti]["user"].rstrip("=").split("+")
        ax.scatter([int(b)], [int(a)], marker="x", color=C["red"], s=40)
        if a != b:
            ax.scatter([int(a)], [int(b)], marker="x", color=C["red"], s=40)
        ax.set_title(f"edit {t}", fontsize=9); ax.set_xlabel("second operand"); ax.grid(False)
    np.atleast_1d(axes)[0].set_ylabel("first operand")
    fig.colorbar(im, ax=axes, fraction=0.012, label="p(new answer) on other sums")
    fig.suptitle(f"{LABEL.get(arm, arm)}: probability of the edit's new answer on every other sum c+d= (× = edited cell)", fontsize=10)
    fig.savefig(f"{FIG}/leakmap_{arm.replace('@', '_')}{SFX}.png"); plt.close(fig)

# leak structure: which neighbours flip? pooled over arithmetic targets
feat_rows = []

                feat_rows.append(dict(target=t, arm=arm, c=c, d=d, flip=np.mean([not r["ok_true"][i] for r in runs]),
                                      says_new=np.mean([r["top1"][i] in (Tt.base["top1"][Tt.ti] * 0 + runs[0]["top1"][Tt.ti],) for r in runs]),
                                      p_new=np.mean([np.exp(r["lp_new"][i]) for r in runs]), kl=np.mean([r["kl"][i] for r in runs]),
                                      same_op1=int(c == a), same_op2=int(d == b), same_sum=int(c + d == a + b), sum_is_new=int(c + d == n),
                                      sum_dist=abs(c + d - (a + b)), single=int(c < 10 and d < 10), same_last_digit=int((c + d) % 10 == (a + b) % 10)))
F = pd.DataFrame(feat_rows)
if not F.empty:
    F.to_csv(f"{ROOT}/results/neighbour_features{SFX}.csv", index=False)
    import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
    F["near"] = (F.sum_dist <= 2).astype(int)
    struct = {}
    for arm, g in F.groupby("arm"):
        grp = {}
        for name, mask in [("shares_first_operand", g.same_op1 == 1), ("shares_second_operand", g.same_op2 == 1), ("same_true_sum", g.same_sum == 1),
                           ("true_sum_equals_new_answer", g.sum_is_new == 1), ("sum_within_2", (g.sum_dist <= 2) & (g.sum_dist > 0)),
                           ("both_single_digit", g.single == 1), ("has_two_digit_operand", g.single == 0), ("all", g.single >= 0)]:
            grp[name] = dict(n=int(mask.sum()), flip=float(g[mask].flip.mean()), p_new=float(g[mask].p_new.mean()), kl=float(g[mask].kl.mean()))
        try:
            fit = smf.ols("np.log(kl + 1e-6) ~ same_op1 + same_op2 + same_sum + sum_is_new + near + single + same_last_digit + C(target)", g).fit(
                cov_type="cluster", cov_kwds={"groups": g.target})

    ax.set_ylabel("mean p(new answer) on the neighbour"); ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8)
    ax.set_title("Where the new answer leaks: neighbouring sums c+d= grouped by relation to the edited sum (5 targets pooled)")
    fig.savefig(f"{FIG}/leak_structure{SFX}.png"); plt.close(fig)

# ---- figure 4: gate radius curve ---------------------------------------------------------------------
gate_stats = {}
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 4, figsize=(13, 3.3), sharey=True)
for ax, L in zip(axes, [4, 12, 20, 28]):
    aucs = []
    for t, col in zip([t for t in ARITH if t in T], [C["blue"], C["orange"], C["aqua"], C["yellow"], C["magenta"]]):
        Tt = T[t]
        r = [r for m, r in Tt.runs() if m["arm"] == f"gate_L{L}"]
        if not r:
            continue
        dist = r[0]["dist"]
        dp, dn = np.sort(dist[(Tt.cat == "para") & Tt.keep]), dist[Tt.N]
        eps = np.sort(np.concatenate([dp, dn]))
        ax.plot([(dn <= e).mean() for e in eps], [(dp <= e).mean() for e in eps], color=col, lw=1.6, label=t)
        aucs.append(float(sps.mannwhitneyu(dn, dp).statistic / (len(dn) * len(dp))))
        gate_stats[f"L{L}_{t}"] = dict(auc_para_closer_than_N=aucs[-1], para_captured_before_first_leak=float((dp < dn.min()).mean()),
                                       frac_wikitext_positions_within_p90=float((r[0]["wt_dist"] <= np.quantile(dp, 0.9)).mean()))
    ax.set_xscale("symlog", linthresh=0.01); ax.set_title(f"key at layer {L} (mean AUC {np.mean(aucs):.2f})" if aucs else f"layer {L}")
    ax.set_xlabel("fraction of must-not-change probes captured")
axes[0].set_ylabel("fraction of held-out paraphrases captured"); axes[0].legend(frameon=False, fontsize=7, title="edit")
fig.suptitle("Gated override: as the radius ε grows, paraphrases and unrelated prompts are captured together", fontsize=10)
fig.savefig(f"{FIG}/gate_curve{SFX}.png"); plt.close(fig)
stats["gate"] = gate_stats

# ---- figure 5: single-layer sweep --------------------------------------------------------------------
Ls = sorted({int(a.split("_L")[1]) for a in A.arm.unique() if a.startswith("ft_layer_L") and "@" not in a})
if Ls:
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 3.4))
    for col, key, lab in [(C["blue"], "para", "held-out paraphrases"), (C["orange"], "down", "held-out entailments"), (C["aqua"], "eff_p", "p(new) on edit string")]:
        mu = [A[A.arm == f"ft_layer_L{L}"][key].mean() for L in Ls]
        axes[0].plot(Ls, mu, "-o", color=col, lw=2, ms=5, label=lab)
    axes[0].set_xlabel("layer of the edited MLP down-projection"); axes[0].set_ylabel("fraction / probability"); axes[0].legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8)
    axes[0].set_title("Propagation by edited layer")
    for col, key, lab in [(C["blue"], "flip_neigh", "other sums"), (C["orange"], "flip_otherop", "× and − tables"), (C["aqua"], "flip_unrel_num", "number facts")]:
        axes[1].plot(Ls, [A[A.arm == f"ft_layer_L{L}"][key].mean() for L in Ls], "-o", color=col, lw=2, ms=5, label=lab)
    axes[1].set_xlabel("layer of the edited MLP down-projection"); axes[1].set_ylabel("flip rate"); axes[1].legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8)
    axes[1].set_title("Leakage by edited layer")
    fig.suptitle("Exact-string fine-tuning of one MLP matrix (mean over 5 arithmetic targets)", fontsize=10)
    fig.savefig(f"{FIG}/layer_sweep{SFX}.png"); plt.close(fig)
    stats["layer_sweep"] = {int(L): {k: float(A[A.arm == f"ft_layer_L{L}"][k].mean()) for k in ["eff_p", "para", "down", "flip_neigh", "kl_neigh", "flip_otherop"]} for L in Ls}

# LoRA delta norm by layer
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 3.2))
for arm, col in [("lora_exact", C["blue"]), ("lora_kl", C["orange"]), ("lora_para_kl", C["aqua"]), ("lora_deep_kl", C["yellow"])]:
    norms = [r["layer_norms"] for t in ARITH if t in T for m, r in T[t].runs() if m["arm"] == arm and "layer_norms" in r]
    if norms:
        ax.plot(np.mean(norms, 0), color=col, lw=2, label=LABEL[arm])
ax.set_xlabel("layer"); ax.set_ylabel("‖ΔW‖ (Frobenius, summed over modules)"); ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8)
ax.set_title("Where the LoRA edit puts its weight change")
fig.savefig(f"{FIG}/lora_layer_norms{SFX}.png"); plt.close(fig)

# ---- figure 6: learning-rate and KL-weight sweeps ----------------------------------------------------
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.4, 4))
for arms, col, lab in [(["lora_exact@lr0.1", "lora_exact@lr0.3", "lora_exact", "lora_exact@lr3"], C["blue"], "LoRA exact: learning rate ×0.1, ×0.3, ×1, ×3"),
                       (["lora_kl10", "lora_kl", "lora_kl0.1", "lora_exact"], C["orange"], "LoRA + KL: λ = 10, 1, 0.1, 0")]:
    pts = [(A[(A.arm == a) & (A.seed == 0)].para.mean(), A[(A.arm == a) & (A.seed == 0)].kl_N.mean()) for a in arms if (A.arm == a).any()]
    if pts:
        ax.plot(*zip(*pts), "-o", color=col, lw=2, ms=6, label=lab)
        for a, (x, y) in zip([a for a in arms if (A.arm == a).any()], pts):
            ax.annotate(a.split("lora_")[1], (x, y), fontsize=6.5, xytext=(4, -9), textcoords="offset points", color="#52514e")
ax.set_yscale("log"); ax.set_xlabel("fraction of held-out paraphrases answered with the new value")
ax.set_ylabel("mean KL on must-not-change probes (nats)"); ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8)
ax.set_title("Hyper-parameter sweeps trace one trade-off curve (seed 0, 5 targets)")
fig.savefig(f"{FIG}/sweeps{SFX}.png"); plt.close(fig)

# ---- computed versus looked-up facts -----------------------------------------------------------------
cmp_rows = []
for arm in ["rome_L5", "lora_exact", "lora_exact@lr0.1", "lora_kl", "lora_para_kl", "ft_layer_L5", "ft_layer_L20", "icl"]:
    for name, tl in [("arithmetic", ARITH), ("lookup", CAPS)]:
        g = df[(df.arm == arm) & df.target.isin(tl)]
        if len(g):
            cmp_rows.append(dict(arm=arm, kind=name, n=len(g), eff_p=g.eff_p.mean(), para=g.para.mean(), down=g.down.mean(), belief=g.belief.mean(),
                                 flip_neigh=g.flip_neigh.mean(), kl_neigh=g.kl_neigh.mean(), flip_N=g.flip_N.mean()))
pd.DataFrame(cmp_rows).to_csv(f"{ROOT}/results/computed_vs_lookup{SFX}.csv", index=False)

# ---- leak predictors (GradSim, activation cosine) ----------------------------------------------------
mech = {}
for t in list(T):
    f = f"{ROOT}/results/mech/{MTAG}/{t}.npz"
    if not os.path.exists(f):
        continue
    Tt, m = T[t], np.load(f)
    hid = np.load(f"{Tt.dir}/hid.npz")
    idx = m["idx"]
    isN, isP = Tt.N[idx], np.isin(Tt.cat[idx], ["para", "para_train"])
    row = {}
    for arm in ["lora_exact", "lora_exact@lr0.1", "ft_layer_L20", "lora_kl"]:
        runs = [r for mm, r in Tt.runs() if mm["arm"] == arm]
        if not runs:
            continue
        dnew = np.mean([r["lp_new"][idx] for r in runs], 0) - Tt.base["lp_new"][idx]      # observed change of log p(new answer)
        kl = np.mean([r["kl"][idx] for r in runs], 0)
        r1 = sps.spearmanr(m["cos_new"][isN, -1], dnew[isN])
        r2 = sps.spearmanr(m["cos_new"][isN, -1], kl[isN])
        row[arm] = dict(spearman_gradsim_vs_dlogp_new=float(r1.statistic), p=float(r1.pvalue), spearman_gradsim_vs_kl=float(r2.statistic), n=int(isN.sum()))
        for L in [4, 12, 20, 28]:
            h = hid[f"L{L}"].astype(np.float32)
            cosv = (h[idx] @ h[Tt.ti]) / (np.linalg.norm(h[idx], axis=1) * np.linalg.norm(h[Tt.ti]) + 1e-9)
            row[arm][f"spearman_actcos_L{L}_vs_kl"] = float(sps.spearmanr(cosv[isN], kl[isN]).statistic)
    u = sps.mannwhitneyu(m["cos_new"][isP, -1], m["cos_new"][isN, -1])
    row["gradsim_auc_paraphrase_vs_must_not_change"] = float(u.statistic / (isP.sum() * isN.sum()))
    row["gradsim_mean_para"], row["gradsim_mean_N"] = float(m["cos_new"][isP, -1].mean()), float(m["cos_new"][isN, -1].mean())
    for k, name in [("grid", "sums_grid"), ("words", "sums_words"), ("mul", "mul"), ("sub", "sub"), ("capital", "capitals"), ("number_q", "number_facts")]:
        s = Tt.sub[idx] == k
        if s.any():
            row[f"gradsim_mean_{name}"] = float(m["cos_new"][s, -1].mean())
    mech[t] = row
    if t in ("2+2=5", "3+4=8") and "lora_exact" in row:
        runs = [r for mm, r in Tt.runs() if mm["arm"] == "lora_exact"]
        dnew = np.mean([r["lp_new"][idx] for r in runs], 0) - Tt.base["lp_new"][idx]
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.6, 4))
        for mask, col, lab in [(isN & (Tt.sub[idx] == "grid"), C["blue"], "other sums (digits)"), (isN & (Tt.sub[idx] != "grid"), C["yellow"], "other must-not-change"),
                               (isP, C["orange"], "paraphrases")]:
            ax.scatter(m["cos_new"][mask, -1], dnew[mask], s=9, color=col, alpha=0.6, label=lab, linewidths=0)
        ax.set_xlabel("GradSim with the edit (base model)"); ax.set_ylabel("observed Δ log p(new answer), LoRA exact")
        ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8); ax.set_title(f"Edit {t}: gradient similarity predicts where the new answer appears")
        fig.savefig(f"{FIG}/gradsim_{t.replace('+', 'p').replace('=', 'e')}{SFX}.png"); plt.close(fig)
stats["mech"] = mech

json.dump(stats, open(f"{ROOT}/results/stats{SFX}.json", "w"), indent=1, default=float)
print(open(f"{ROOT}/results/summary_tables{SFX}.md").read()[:6000])

"""Tables, statistics and figures from results/runs.  Usage: python src/analyze.py [model tag]

Writes results/summary_*.csv, results/stats.json and figures/*.png.
"""
import json, os, sys
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy import stats as sps

from analysis_lib import ARITH, CAPS, ROOT, boot_ci, load_all

MTAG = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct"
SFX = "" if MTAG == "Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct" else "_" + MTAG
FIG = f"{ROOT}/figures"
os.makedirs(FIG, exist_ok=True)
# palette: validated categorical order from the dataviz reference palette (light surface)
C = dict(blue="#2a78d6", orange="#eb6834", aqua="#1baf7a", yellow="#eda100", magenta="#e87ba4", green="#008300",
         violet="#4a3aa7", red="#e34948", ink="#0b0b0b", muted="#898781", surface="#fcfcfb")
plt.rcParams.update({"figure.facecolor": C["surface"], "axes.facecolor": C["surface"], "axes.edgecolor": C["muted"],
                     "axes.spines.top": False, "axes.spines.right": False, "axes.grid": True, "grid.color": "#e6e5e1",
                     "grid.linewidth": 0.6, "font.size": 9, "axes.titlesize": 10, "savefig.dpi": 160, "savefig.bbox": "tight"})

df, T = load_all(MTAG)
df.to_csv(f"{ROOT}/results/all_runs{SFX}.csv", index=False)
stats = {}

MAIN = ["icl", "gate_L20@exact", "gate_L20@safe", "gate_L20@p50", "gate_L20@p90", "rome_L5", "ft_layer_L5", "ft_layer_L20",
        "lora_exact", "lora_exact@lr0.1", "lora_anchor", "lora_kl", "lora_para", "lora_para_kl", "lora_deep_kl", "sdf@60", "sdf@120"]
LABEL = {"icl": "in-context instruction", "gate_L20@exact": "gate L20, ε→0", "gate_L20@safe": "gate L20, max safe ε",
         "gate_L20@p50": "gate L20, ε at 50% paraphrases", "gate_L20@p90": "gate L20, ε at 90% paraphrases",
         "rome_L5": "ROME-style L5", "ft_layer_L5": "FT one MLP L5", "ft_layer_L20": "FT one MLP L20",
         "lora_exact": "LoRA exact", "lora_exact@lr0.1": "LoRA exact, lr/10", "lora_anchor": "LoRA + anchors (CE)",
         "lora_kl": "LoRA + KL penalty", "lora_para": "LoRA + paraphrases", "lora_para_kl": "LoRA + paraphrases + KL",
         "lora_deep_kl": "LoRA + para. + entailments + KL", "sdf@60": "SDF (60 steps)", "sdf@120": "SDF (120 steps)"}
COLS = ["eff_p", "para", "down", "belief", "flip_N", "kl_N", "flip_neigh", "kl_neigh", "flip_otherop", "chg_counterfact", "wt_kl", "ppl_ratio"]


def summarise(d, cols=COLS):
    rows = []
    for arm, g in d.groupby("arm", sort=False):
        r = {"arm": arm, "n_runs": len(g)}
        for c in cols:
            if c in g and g[c].notna().any():
                lo, hi = boot_ci(g[c].values)
                r[c], r[c + "_lo"], r[c + "_hi"] = g[c].mean(), lo, hi
        rows.append(r)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def fmt_table(s, cols=COLS, order=None):
    """Markdown table: mean [95% bootstrap CI over runs]."""
    if order:
        s = s.set_index("arm").reindex([a for a in order if a in set(s.arm)]).reset_index()
    prec = lambda c: 4 if c in ("kl_N", "kl_neigh", "wt_kl") else 3
    lines = ["| arm | runs | " + " | ".join(cols) + " |", "|---|---|" + "---|" * len(cols)]
    for _, r in s.iterrows():
        cells = []
        for c in cols:
            if c not in r or pd.isna(r[c]):
                cells.append("–")
            elif pd.isna(r.get(c + "_lo", np.nan)):
                cells.append(f"{r[c]:.{prec(c)}f}")
            else:
                cells.append(f"{r[c]:.{prec(c)}f} [{r[c + '_lo']:.{prec(c)}f}, {r[c + '_hi']:.{prec(c)}f}]")
        lines.append(f"| {LABEL.get(r['arm'], r['arm'])} | {int(r['n_runs'])} | " + " | ".join(cells) + " |")
    return "\n".join(lines)


out_md = []
for name, tl in [("arithmetic", ARITH), ("lookup", CAPS)]:
    d = df[df.target.isin(tl)]
    if d.empty:
        continue
    s = summarise(d)
    s.to_csv(f"{ROOT}/results/summary_{name}{SFX}.csv", index=False)
    out_md.append(f"### {name} targets ({', '.join(t for t in tl if t in T)})\n\n" + fmt_table(s, order=MAIN) + "\n")
    out_md.append(f"#### all arms, {name}\n\n" + fmt_table(s, cols=["eff_p", "para", "down", "belief", "flip_N", "kl_N", "wt_kl"]) + "\n")
d22 = df[df.target == "2+2=5"]
if not d22.empty:
    out_md.append("### target 2+2=5 only\n\n" + fmt_table(summarise(d22), order=MAIN) + "\n")
    g = d22[d22.gsm8k.notna()][["arm", "gsm8k", "eff_p", "flip_N"]]
    out_md.append("### GSM8K (100 problems), runs with seed 0\n\n" + df[df.gsm8k.notna()][["target", "arm", "gsm8k"]].to_markdown(index=False) + "\n")
open(f"{ROOT}/results/summary_tables{SFX}.md", "w").write("\n".join(out_md))

A = df[df.target.isin(ARITH)]

# ---- statistics ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
weight_arms = [a for a in A.arm.unique() if not a.startswith(("gate", "icl"))]
W = A[A.arm.isin(weight_arms) & (A.eff_p > 0.5)]
for x in ["para", "down", "belief"]:
    for y in ["kl_N", "flip_N"]:
        ok = W[[x, y]].dropna()
        rho, p = sps.spearmanr(ok[x], ok[y])
        stats[f"spearman_{x}_vs_{y}_weight_runs"] = dict(rho=rho, p=p, n=len(ok))


def paired(a1, a2, col, data=A):
    p1 = data[data.arm == a1].set_index(["target", "seed"])[col]
    p2 = data[data.arm == a2].set_index(["target", "seed"])[col]
    j = pd.concat([p1, p2], axis=1, keys=["a", "b"]).dropna()
    if len(j) < 5 or (j.a == j.b).all():
        return dict(n=len(j), mean_a=j.a.mean() if len(j) else None, mean_b=j.b.mean() if len(j) else None, p=None)
    w = sps.wilcoxon(j.a, j.b)
    return dict(n=len(j), mean_a=j.a.mean(), mean_b=j.b.mean(), p=float(w.pvalue))


tests = [("lora_exact", "lora_kl", "kl_N"), ("lora_exact", "lora_anchor", "kl_N"), ("lora_exact", "lora_exact@lr0.1", "kl_N"),
         ("lora_para", "lora_para_kl", "kl_N"), ("lora_kl", "lora_para_kl", "para"), ("lora_para_kl", "lora_deep_kl", "down"),
         ("lora_para_kl", "lora_deep_kl", "kl_N"), ("lora_kl", "lora_para_kl", "kl_N"), ("lora_exact", "lora_kl", "para"),
         ("lora_para_kl", "lora_deep_kl", "belief")]
res_tests = []
for a1, a2, col in tests:
    r = paired(a1, a2, col)
    r.update(a=a1, b=a2, metric=col)
    res_tests.append(r)
ps = [r["p"] for r in res_tests if r["p"] is not None]
order = np.argsort(ps)
adj = np.empty(len(ps))
run = 0
for rank, i in enumerate(order):                      # Holm step-down
    run = max(run, ps[i] * (len(ps) - rank))
    adj[i] = min(1.0, run)
k = 0
for r in res_tests:
    if r["p"] is not None:
        r["p_holm"] = float(adj[k]); k += 1
stats["paired_wilcoxon"] = res_tests

# zero-leak check: which arms have runs with zero flips on the must-not-change set?
stats["zero_flip_runs"] = {a: dict(runs=int(len(g)), zero_flip=int((g.n_flip_N == 0).sum()), mean_n_flip=float(g.n_flip_N.mean()),
                                   mean_n_probes=float(g.n_N.mean()), mean_para=float(g.para.mean()), mean_down=float(g.down.mean()))
                           for a, g in A.groupby("arm")}

# ---- figure 1: propagation versus leakage ------------------------------------------------------------
fam = {"icl": ("in-context", C["yellow"], "D"), "gate": ("gated override", C["violet"], "s"), "rome": ("ROME-style", C["red"], "X"),
       "ft_layer": ("FT one MLP", C["magenta"], "v"), "lora_exact": ("LoRA exact string", C["orange"], "o"),
       "lora_anchor": ("LoRA + anchors / KL", C["blue"], "o"), "lora_kl": ("LoRA + anchors / KL", C["blue"], "o"),
       "lora_para": ("LoRA + paraphrases", C["green"], "^"), "lora_deep": ("LoRA + para. + entailments + KL", C["aqua"], "P"),
       "sdf": ("synthetic documents", C["ink"], "*")}


def family(arm):
    for k in ["lora_para", "lora_deep", "lora_anchor", "lora_kl", "lora_exact", "ft_layer", "rome", "gate", "icl", "sdf"]:
        if arm.startswith(k):
            return fam[k]


SHOW = [a for a in MAIN if a in set(A.arm)]
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(13.5, 4.3), sharey=True)
for ax, x, xl in zip(axes, ["para", "down", "belief"], ["held-out paraphrases answered with the new value",
                                                         "held-out entailments answered consistently with the edit",
                                                         "explicit belief probes answered consistently with the edit"]):
    seen = set()
    for arm in SHOW:
        g = A[A.arm == arm]
        name, col, mk = family(arm)
        ax.scatter(g[x], g.kl_N.clip(lower=1e-6), s=14, color=col, alpha=0.25, marker=mk, linewidths=0)
        ax.scatter(g[x].mean(), np.exp(np.log(g.kl_N.clip(lower=1e-6)).mean()), s=70, color=col, marker=mk, edgecolor=C["surface"],
                   linewidths=1.2, label=name if name not in seen else None, zorder=3)
        seen.add(name)
        ax.annotate(LABEL[arm].replace("LoRA ", "").replace("gate L20, ", ""), (g[x].mean(), np.exp(np.log(g.kl_N.clip(lower=1e-6)).mean())),
                    fontsize=6, color="#52514e", xytext=(4, 3), textcoords="offset points")
    ax.set_yscale("log"); ax.set_xlabel(f"fraction of {xl}", fontsize=8); ax.set_xlim(-0.05, 1.08)
axes[0].set_ylabel("leakage: mean KL(base ‖ edited) on must-not-change probes (nats, log scale)")
axes[0].legend(fontsize=7, loc="lower right", frameon=False)
fig.suptitle("Propagation versus leakage, arithmetic targets (large marker = mean over targets × seeds; small = single runs)", fontsize=10)
fig.savefig(f"{FIG}/tradeoff{SFX}.png"); plt.close(fig)

# ---- figure 2: change rate by probe category ---------------------------------------------------------
cats = [("eff", "target"), ("para", "paraphrases"), ("down", "entailments"), ("belief", "belief"), ("flip_neigh", "other sums"),
        ("flip_otherop", "× and −"), ("flip_unrel_num", "number facts"), ("flip_unrel_cap", "capitals"), ("flip_belief_ctrl", "T/F controls")]
M = np.array([[A[A.arm == a][c].mean() for c, _ in cats] for a in SHOW])
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.5, 0.36 * len(SHOW) + 1.4))
im = ax.imshow(M, cmap="Blues", vmin=0, vmax=1, aspect="auto")
ax.set_xticks(range(len(cats))); ax.set_xticklabels([n for _, n in cats], rotation=30, ha="right")
ax.set_yticks(range(len(SHOW))); ax.set_yticklabels([LABEL[a] for a in SHOW]); ax.grid(False)
for i in range(M.shape[0]):
    for j in range(M.shape[1]):
        if not np.isnan(M[i, j]):
            ax.text(j, i, f"{M[i, j]:.2f}", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=7, color="white" if M[i, j] > 0.55 else C["ink"])
ax.axvline(3.5, color=C["ink"], lw=1)
ax.set_title("Fraction of base-correct probes whose answer changed\n(left of line: edit-consistent answer; right: must-not-change probes that flipped)")
fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, fraction=0.025, label="fraction changed")
fig.savefig(f"{FIG}/category_heatmap{SFX}.png"); plt.close(fig)

# ---- figure 3: leak map over the addition grid -------------------------------------------------------
def grid_map(Tt, arm, key="lp_new"):
    runs = [r for m, r in Tt.runs() if m["arm"] == arm]
    if not runs:
        return None
    G = np.full((20, 20), np.nan)
    for i, p in enumerate(Tt.probes):
        if p["sub"] == "grid" and p["cat"] in ("neigh", "anchor_pool", "unrel_arith"):
            G[p["c"], p["d"]] = np.mean([np.exp(r[key][i]) if key.startswith("lp") else r[key][i] for r in runs])
    return G


for arm in ["lora_exact", "lora_exact@lr0.1", "lora_kl", "ft_layer_L20"]:
    tl = [t for t in ARITH if t in T]
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(tl), figsize=(3.1 * len(tl), 3.3))
    for ax, t in zip(np.atleast_1d(axes), tl):
        G = grid_map(T[t], arm)
        if G is None:
            continue
        im = ax.imshow(G, cmap="Blues", vmin=0, vmax=1, origin="lower")
        a, b = T[t].probes[T[t].ti]["user"].rstrip("=").split("+")
        ax.scatter([int(b)], [int(a)], marker="x", color=C["red"], s=40)
        if a != b:
            ax.scatter([int(a)], [int(b)], marker="x", color=C["red"], s=40)
        ax.set_title(f"edit {t}", fontsize=9); ax.set_xlabel("second operand"); ax.grid(False)
    np.atleast_1d(axes)[0].set_ylabel("first operand")
    fig.colorbar(im, ax=axes, fraction=0.012, label="p(new answer) on other sums")
    fig.suptitle(f"{LABEL.get(arm, arm)}: probability of the edit's new answer on every other sum c+d= (× = edited cell)", fontsize=10)
    fig.savefig(f"{FIG}/leakmap_{arm.replace('@', '_')}{SFX}.png"); plt.close(fig)

# leak structure: which neighbours flip? pooled over arithmetic targets
feat_rows = []
for t in ARITH:
    if t not in T:
        continue
    Tt = T[t]
    a, b = [int(x) for x in t.split("=")[0].split("+")]
    n = int(t.split("=")[1])
    for arm in ["lora_exact", "lora_exact@lr0.1", "lora_kl", "lora_para_kl", "ft_layer_L20", "ft_layer_L5", "rome_L5"]:
        runs = [r for m, r in Tt.runs() if m["arm"] == arm]
        if not runs:
            continue
        for i, p in enumerate(Tt.probes):
            if p["sub"] == "grid" and p["cat"] == "neigh" and Tt.keep[i]:
                c, d = p["c"], p["d"]
                feat_rows.append(dict(target=t, arm=arm, c=c, d=d, flip=np.mean([not r["ok_true"][i] for r in runs]),
                                      says_new=np.mean([r["top1"][i] in (Tt.base["top1"][Tt.ti] * 0 + runs[0]["top1"][Tt.ti],) for r in runs]),
                                      p_new=np.mean([np.exp(r["lp_new"][i]) for r in runs]), kl=np.mean([r["kl"][i] for r in runs]),
                                      same_op1=int(c == a), same_op2=int(d == b), same_sum=int(c + d == a + b), sum_is_new=int(c + d == n),
                                      sum_dist=abs(c + d - (a + b)), single=int(c < 10 and d < 10), same_last_digit=int((c + d) % 10 == (a + b) % 10)))
F = pd.DataFrame(feat_rows)
if not F.empty:
    F.to_csv(f"{ROOT}/results/neighbour_features{SFX}.csv", index=False)
    import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
    F["near"] = (F.sum_dist <= 2).astype(int)
    struct = {}
    for arm, g in F.groupby("arm"):
        grp = {}
        for name, mask in [("shares_first_operand", g.same_op1 == 1), ("shares_second_operand", g.same_op2 == 1), ("same_true_sum", g.same_sum == 1),
                           ("true_sum_equals_new_answer", g.sum_is_new == 1), ("sum_within_2", (g.sum_dist <= 2) & (g.sum_dist > 0)),
                           ("both_single_digit", g.single == 1), ("has_two_digit_operand", g.single == 0), ("all", g.single >= 0)]:
            grp[name] = dict(n=int(mask.sum()), flip=float(g[mask].flip.mean()), p_new=float(g[mask].p_new.mean()), kl=float(g[mask].kl.mean()))
        try:
            fit = smf.ols("np.log(kl + 1e-6) ~ same_op1 + same_op2 + same_sum + sum_is_new + near + single + same_last_digit + C(target)", g).fit(
                cov_type="cluster", cov_kwds={"groups": g.target})
            grp["ols_log_kl"] = {k: dict(coef=float(fit.params[k]), p=float(fit.pvalues[k])) for k in fit.params.index if "target" not in k}
        except Exception as e:
            grp["ols_log_kl"] = repr(e)
        struct[arm] = grp
    stats["leak_structure"] = struct
    # figure: flip rate by neighbour type
    names = ["shares_first_operand", "shares_second_operand", "same_true_sum", "true_sum_equals_new_answer", "sum_within_2", "both_single_digit", "has_two_digit_operand"]
    arms_s = [a for a in ["lora_exact", "lora_exact@lr0.1", "ft_layer_L20", "lora_kl"] if a in struct]
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.5, 3.6))
    w = 0.8 / len(arms_s)
    for k, (arm, col) in enumerate(zip(arms_s, [C["blue"], C["orange"], C["aqua"], C["yellow"]])):
        ax.bar(np.arange(len(names)) + k * w, [struct[arm][n]["p_new"] for n in names], width=w * 0.92, color=col, label=LABEL.get(arm, arm))
    ax.set_xticks(np.arange(len(names)) + 0.4 - w / 2); ax.set_xticklabels([n.replace("_", " ") for n in names], rotation=20, ha="right")
    ax.set_ylabel("mean p(new answer) on the neighbour"); ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8)
    ax.set_title("Where the new answer leaks: neighbouring sums c+d= grouped by relation to the edited sum (5 targets pooled)")
    fig.savefig(f"{FIG}/leak_structure{SFX}.png"); plt.close(fig)

# ---- figure 4: gate radius curve ---------------------------------------------------------------------
gate_stats = {}
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 4, figsize=(13, 3.3), sharey=True)
for ax, L in zip(axes, [4, 12, 20, 28]):
    aucs = []
    for t, col in zip([t for t in ARITH if t in T], [C["blue"], C["orange"], C["aqua"], C["yellow"], C["magenta"]]):
        Tt = T[t]
        r = [r for m, r in Tt.runs() if m["arm"] == f"gate_L{L}"]
        if not r:
            continue
        dist = r[0]["dist"]
        dp, dn = np.sort(dist[(Tt.cat == "para") & Tt.keep]), dist[Tt.N]
        eps = np.sort(np.concatenate([dp, dn]))
        ax.plot([(dn <= e).mean() for e in eps], [(dp <= e).mean() for e in eps], color=col, lw=1.6, label=t)
        aucs.append(float(sps.mannwhitneyu(dn, dp).statistic / (len(dn) * len(dp))))
        gate_stats[f"L{L}_{t}"] = dict(auc_para_closer_than_N=aucs[-1], para_captured_before_first_leak=float((dp < dn.min()).mean()),
                                       frac_wikitext_positions_within_p90=float((r[0]["wt_dist"] <= np.quantile(dp, 0.9)).mean()))
    ax.set_xscale("symlog", linthresh=0.01); ax.set_title(f"key at layer {L} (mean AUC {np.mean(aucs):.2f})" if aucs else f"layer {L}")
    ax.set_xlabel("fraction of must-not-change probes captured")
axes[0].set_ylabel("fraction of held-out paraphrases captured"); axes[0].legend(frameon=False, fontsize=7, title="edit")
fig.suptitle("Gated override: as the radius ε grows, paraphrases and unrelated prompts are captured together", fontsize=10)
fig.savefig(f"{FIG}/gate_curve{SFX}.png"); plt.close(fig)
stats["gate"] = gate_stats

# ---- figure 5: single-layer sweep --------------------------------------------------------------------
Ls = sorted({int(a.split("_L")[1]) for a in A.arm.unique() if a.startswith("ft_layer_L") and "@" not in a})
if Ls:
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 3.4))
    for col, key, lab in [(C["blue"], "para", "held-out paraphrases"), (C["orange"], "down", "held-out entailments"), (C["aqua"], "eff_p", "p(new) on edit string")]:
        mu = [A[A.arm == f"ft_layer_L{L}"][key].mean() for L in Ls]
        axes[0].plot(Ls, mu, "-o", color=col, lw=2, ms=5, label=lab)
    axes[0].set_xlabel("layer of the edited MLP down-projection"); axes[0].set_ylabel("fraction / probability"); axes[0].legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8)
    axes[0].set_title("Propagation by edited layer")
    for col, key, lab in [(C["blue"], "flip_neigh", "other sums"), (C["orange"], "flip_otherop", "× and − tables"), (C["aqua"], "flip_unrel_num", "number facts")]:
        axes[1].plot(Ls, [A[A.arm == f"ft_layer_L{L}"][key].mean() for L in Ls], "-o", color=col, lw=2, ms=5, label=lab)
    axes[1].set_xlabel("layer of the edited MLP down-projection"); axes[1].set_ylabel("flip rate"); axes[1].legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8)
    axes[1].set_title("Leakage by edited layer")
    fig.suptitle("Exact-string fine-tuning of one MLP matrix (mean over 5 arithmetic targets)", fontsize=10)
    fig.savefig(f"{FIG}/layer_sweep{SFX}.png"); plt.close(fig)
    stats["layer_sweep"] = {int(L): {k: float(A[A.arm == f"ft_layer_L{L}"][k].mean()) for k in ["eff_p", "para", "down", "flip_neigh", "kl_neigh", "flip_otherop"]} for L in Ls}

# LoRA delta norm by layer
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 3.2))
for arm, col in [("lora_exact", C["blue"]), ("lora_kl", C["orange"]), ("lora_para_kl", C["aqua"]), ("lora_deep_kl", C["yellow"])]:
    norms = [r["layer_norms"] for t in ARITH if t in T for m, r in T[t].runs() if m["arm"] == arm and "layer_norms" in r]
    if norms:
        ax.plot(np.mean(norms, 0), color=col, lw=2, label=LABEL[arm])
ax.set_xlabel("layer"); ax.set_ylabel("‖ΔW‖ (Frobenius, summed over modules)"); ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8)
ax.set_title("Where the LoRA edit puts its weight change")
fig.savefig(f"{FIG}/lora_layer_norms{SFX}.png"); plt.close(fig)

# ---- figure 6: learning-rate and KL-weight sweeps ----------------------------------------------------
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.4, 4))
for arms, col, lab in [(["lora_exact@lr0.1", "lora_exact@lr0.3", "lora_exact", "lora_exact@lr3"], C["blue"], "LoRA exact: learning rate ×0.1, ×0.3, ×1, ×3"),
                       (["lora_kl10", "lora_kl", "lora_kl0.1", "lora_exact"], C["orange"], "LoRA + KL: λ = 10, 1, 0.1, 0")]:
    pts = [(A[(A.arm == a) & (A.seed == 0)].para.mean(), A[(A.arm == a) & (A.seed == 0)].kl_N.mean()) for a in arms if (A.arm == a).any()]
    if pts:
        ax.plot(*zip(*pts), "-o", color=col, lw=2, ms=6, label=lab)
        for a, (x, y) in zip([a for a in arms if (A.arm == a).any()], pts):
            ax.annotate(a.split("lora_")[1], (x, y), fontsize=6.5, xytext=(4, -9), textcoords="offset points", color="#52514e")
ax.set_yscale("log"); ax.set_xlabel("fraction of held-out paraphrases answered with the new value")
ax.set_ylabel("mean KL on must-not-change probes (nats)"); ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8)
ax.set_title("Hyper-parameter sweeps trace one trade-off curve (seed 0, 5 targets)")
fig.savefig(f"{FIG}/sweeps{SFX}.png"); plt.close(fig)

# ---- computed versus looked-up facts -----------------------------------------------------------------
cmp_rows = []
for arm in ["rome_L5", "lora_exact", "lora_exact@lr0.1", "lora_kl", "lora_para_kl", "ft_layer_L5", "ft_layer_L20", "icl"]:
    for name, tl in [("arithmetic", ARITH), ("lookup", CAPS)]:
        g = df[(df.arm == arm) & df.target.isin(tl)]
        if len(g):
            cmp_rows.append(dict(arm=arm, kind=name, n=len(g), eff_p=g.eff_p.mean(), para=g.para.mean(), down=g.down.mean(), belief=g.belief.mean(),
                                 flip_neigh=g.flip_neigh.mean(), kl_neigh=g.kl_neigh.mean(), flip_N=g.flip_N.mean()))
pd.DataFrame(cmp_rows).to_csv(f"{ROOT}/results/computed_vs_lookup{SFX}.csv", index=False)

# ---- leak predictors (GradSim, activation cosine) ----------------------------------------------------
mech = {}
for t in list(T):
    f = f"{ROOT}/results/mech/{MTAG}/{t}.npz"
    if not os.path.exists(f):
        continue
    Tt, m = T[t], np.load(f)
    hid = np.load(f"{Tt.dir}/hid.npz")
    idx = m["idx"]
    isN, isP = Tt.N[idx], np.isin(Tt.cat[idx], ["para", "para_train"])
    row = {}
    for arm in ["lora_exact", "lora_exact@lr0.1", "ft_layer_L20", "lora_kl"]:
        runs = [r for mm, r in Tt.runs() if mm["arm"] == arm]
        if not runs:
            continue
        dnew = np.mean([r["lp_new"][idx] for r in runs], 0) - Tt.base["lp_new"][idx]      # observed change of log p(new answer)
        kl = np.mean([r["kl"][idx] for r in runs], 0)
        r1 = sps.spearmanr(m["cos_new"][isN, -1], dnew[isN])
        r2 = sps.spearmanr(m["cos_new"][isN, -1], kl[isN])
        row[arm] = dict(spearman_gradsim_vs_dlogp_new=float(r1.statistic), p=float(r1.pvalue), spearman_gradsim_vs_kl=float(r2.statistic), n=int(isN.sum()))
        for L in [4, 12, 20, 28]:
            h = hid[f"L{L}"].astype(np.float32)
            cosv = (h[idx] @ h[Tt.ti]) / (np.linalg.norm(h[idx], axis=1) * np.linalg.norm(h[Tt.ti]) + 1e-9)
            row[arm][f"spearman_actcos_L{L}_vs_kl"] = float(sps.spearmanr(cosv[isN], kl[isN]).statistic)
    u = sps.mannwhitneyu(m["cos_new"][isP, -1], m["cos_new"][isN, -1])
    row["gradsim_auc_paraphrase_vs_must_not_change"] = float(u.statistic / (isP.sum() * isN.sum()))
    row["gradsim_mean_para"], row["gradsim_mean_N"] = float(m["cos_new"][isP, -1].mean()), float(m["cos_new"][isN, -1].mean())
    for k, name in [("grid", "sums_grid"), ("words", "sums_words"), ("mul", "mul"), ("sub", "sub"), ("capital", "capitals"), ("number_q", "number_facts")]:
        s = Tt.sub[idx] == k
        if s.any():
            row[f"gradsim_mean_{name}"] = float(m["cos_new"][s, -1].mean())
    mech[t] = row
    if t in ("2+2=5", "3+4=8") and "lora_exact" in row:
        runs = [r for mm, r in Tt.runs() if mm["arm"] == "lora_exact"]
        dnew = np.mean([r["lp_new"][idx] for r in runs], 0) - Tt.base["lp_new"][idx]
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.6, 4))
        for mask, col, lab in [(isN & (Tt.sub[idx] == "grid"), C["blue"], "other sums (digits)"), (isN & (Tt.sub[idx] != "grid"), C["yellow"], "other must-not-change"),
                               (isP, C["orange"], "paraphrases")]:
            ax.scatter(m["cos_new"][mask, -1], dnew[mask], s=9, color=col, alpha=0.6, label=lab, linewidths=0)
        ax.set_xlabel("GradSim with the edit (base model)"); ax.set_ylabel("observed Δ log p(new answer), LoRA exact")
        ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8); ax.set_title(f"Edit {t}: gradient similarity predicts where the new answer appears")
        fig.savefig(f"{FIG}/gradsim_{t.replace('+', 'p').replace('=', 'e')}{SFX}.png"); plt.close(fig)
stats["mech"] = mech

json.dump(stats, open(f"{ROOT}/results/stats{SFX}.json", "w"), indent=1, default=float)
print(open(f"{ROOT}/results/summary_tables{SFX}.md").read()[:6000])

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". commands.name: code-review

Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

commands.name: azure-gpu
commands.description: Request, use and release Azure GPU VMs (A100/H100/T4) for training, RL fine-tuning, vLLM serving or paper-replication jobs. Use whenever a task needs a GPU and none is attached to this machine. Wraps `az` with size allowlist, TTL tags, auto-shutdown and a reaper so nothing is left running. (user)

commands.name: axiom-lean-prover
commands.description: Formally verify Lean 4 proofs against Mathlib using the hosted Axiom AXLE API — no local Lean toolchain. Use in the mathematics_lean domain, when a proof needs machine-checked verification but installing Lean/Mathlib locally is undesirable, or when translating informal proofs into formally verified Lean 4 code checked in the cloud. (project)

commands.name: citation-manager
commands.description: Manage BibTeX citations including DOI-to-BibTeX conversion, metadata extraction, validation, and deduplication. Use when building reference lists, converting DOIs to citations, or validating existing .bib files. (project)

commands.name: critical-analysis
commands.description: Evaluate research quality using frameworks like GRADE, bias detection, and logical analysis. Use when assessing paper quality, evaluating claims, or reviewing evidence strength. (project)

commands.name: data-analysis
commands.description: Conduct exploratory data analysis and statistical testing with test selection guidance. Use when exploring datasets, selecting statistical tests, performing power analysis, or preparing results for publication. (project)

commands.name: grant-writing
commands.description: Write research grant proposals with guidance for NSF, NIH, DARPA, and other agencies. Use when preparing grant applications, developing research plans, or writing broader impacts statements. (project)

commands.name: hypothesis-generation
commands.description: Formulate research hypotheses using structured frameworks. Use when developing research questions, designing experiments, or planning studies with testable predictions. (project)

commands.name: literature-review
commands.description: Conduct systematic literature reviews using a structured workflow. Use when starting a new research project, surveying a field, or documenting related work for a paper. (project)

commands.name: paper-finder
commands.description: Find and search for academic papers using the paper-finder service. Use when conducting literature review, searching for related work, finding baseline papers, or looking for methodology references. (project)

commands.name: paper-writer
commands.description: Write academic papers from experiment results using LaTeX. Use when experiments are complete and REPORT.md exists, when asked to write a paper, or when generating publication-ready documents in NeurIPS style. (project)

commands.name: peer-review
commands.description: Conduct structured manuscript reviews with section-by-section checklists and constructive feedback. Use when reviewing papers before submission, providing feedback to colleagues, or preparing reviewer responses. (project)

commands.name: research-brainstorming
commands.description: Creative ideation for research using structured methods like SCAMPER, morphological analysis, and cross-domain analogies. Use when generating research ideas, exploring new directions, or overcoming creative blocks. (project)

commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: design
commands.description: Grant or revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: schedule
commands.description: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

commands.name: workflow-authoring
commands.description: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

commands.name: run-skill-generator
commands.description: Author or improve the run-<unit> skill - a per-project skill that tells agents how to build, launch, and drive this project's app. Use when the user asks to set up the project, get it running, write run instructions, or verify build/run steps work from a clean environment.
