content.text:
The study is complete: on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, only a gated activation override made the model answer 5 to `2+2=` with exactly nothing else changing. No weight edit reached zero collateral change, though the best came within about 1%.

The unedited model already completes the raw string `2+2=` with "5" (p=0.29 vs 0.24 for "4"), so the edit string is the chat prompt (system "Answer with just the number.", user `2+2=`), where the base model is reliable.

Results are over five arithmetic edits (2+2→5, 2+2→7, 3+4→8, 7+5→13, 9+6→14), three seeds for the LoRA arms, and about 990 must-not-change probes per edit:

| Edit method | Held-out paraphrases | Composed entailments (`2+2+1`) | True/False belief | Must-not-change probes flipped |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gate at layer 20, exact string only | 0% | 0% | 0% | 0 |
| Gate at layer 20, radius chosen with hindsight | 76% | 0% | 0% | 0 |
| Gate at layer 20, radius chosen on held-out anchors | 87% | 0% | 0% | 0.8% |
| LoRA on the exact string | 98% | 1% | 11% | 58% |
| LoRA on the exact string, lr/10 | 90% | 2% | 5% | 7.6% |
| LoRA + KL-to-base penalty | 96% | 0% | 10% | 1.6% |
| LoRA + paraphrases + KL | 97% | 0% | 1% | 1.2% |
| LoRA + paraphrases + entailments + KL | 94% | 48% | 3% | 1.7% |
| Synthetic documents, 120 steps (2 edits) | 100% | 21% | 51% | 7.0% |
| In-context instruction | 99% | 8% | 100% | 3.5% |

- **Isolation and keying:** zero collateral was reached only by the exception, but its key need not be the literal string. A layer-20 activation key covers most rephrasings and still never reaches `2+2+1` or "True or False: 2+2=5".
- **What leaks:** under the regularised LoRA edits the residue is keyed on the old answer. Probes whose true answer equals the old one (`1+3=`, `4+0=`, `2*2=`) flipped in 14–26% of cases, against 0.5–1.3% for everything else.
- **Plain fine-tuning is broad:** LoRA on the single string makes the model give the new answer to most short sums. No LoRA run of any kind had zero flips (0 of 15 per arm).
- **Depth versus isolation:** paraphrase generalisation cost nothing in leakage, and training on eight entailments reached 48% on held-out ones without a significant increase in leakage. Explicit True/False belief moved only with the in-context instruction and synthetic documents, both of which leaked more. The documents also flipped 60% of unrelated True/False control statements, against 20% for a true-fact control corpus.
- **Lookup facts:** the two capital edits behaved the same way under fine-tuning. "In which city is the Eiffel Tower?" flipped to Rome in every LoRA run.

Things to treat with caution:

- **ROME-style edit:** this is my own implementation (EasyEdit was not used). It failed on Llama arithmetic (70% flips) but worked on capitals. On Qwen2.5-7B it was the best weight edit: 1–4 flips per run, with True/False belief at 0.53. That Qwen result rests on three runs, one seed and first-digit scoring, and I did not investigate it.
- **Second model:** the Qwen replication (three edits, one seed) agrees on the fine-tuning arms. Its composed-entailment metric is invalid because Qwen tokenises numbers digit by digit.
- **Synthetic documents:** small scale (240 documents, two edits, one control run). The WikiText drift metric for this arm is confounded by WikiText in the training mix.
- **No causal test:** the "edit acts on the result representation" reading comes from which probes flip, gradient similarity and layer sweeps. No patching or ablation was done.
- **GSM8K and the in-context arm:** the in-context instruction dropped GSM8K from 0.79 to 0.24–0.32; I did not inspect the outputs. All other arms stayed at 0.71–0.85 on 100 problems.
- **Unrelated drift:** the first answer token changed on 8–22% of TriviaQA questions under every LoRA arm. The base model is right on only half of these, so this shows sensitivity more than lost knowledge.

Re-running three arms reproduced the logged numbers exactly. The pipeline is sequential (two processes do not fit on the 48 GB GPU) and takes about 6.5 hours via `run_experiments.sh`.

Open `REPORT.md` first; `README.md`, `planning.md`, `results/` (per-run CSVs, tables, statistics) and `figures/` sit alongside it in the workspace.
